answer: Weight follows a trellis of funding provenance: each identity posts a copper bond whose funding root is published, and identities sharing one root pay a bonding-curve fee that squares with each extra head. A lone agent crosses that ocean of cost once; an operator funding n clones from a single root pays roughly n², because the trellis exposes the shared root and prices every new branch higher than the last. A fresh root earns no shortcut — it must itself build tenure before its bonds count.
